requirement:
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text,
except for structural assessments under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.

An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.

These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every testable obligation in `requirements.references.authoring_inputs`. One clause has no dedicated test: the prohibition on describing reference links as proof of completeness. That clause is not testable in the sense the criteria require, so I did not count it as a gap.

I mapped each obligation to a test and its assertions. All tests are in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` unless noted.

- **The subject's `{cite}` contributes the cited declaration's complete text.**
  - `mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` asserts that `requirements.base` is supplied and that `requirements.distant` is not.
  - `only_edges_leaving_the_subject_contribute_inputs` asserts that `requirements.base` is supplied when `ready` cites it.
  - `cited_built_ins_contribute_their_text_and_fixmes_in_own_sites_do_not` asserts that a cited built-in contributes its fixed text once and that a cited `requirements.other` declaration is supplied.
- **A requirement or example declaration with `{impl}` or `{test}` to the subject contributes its complete declaration.**
  - The bundle test asserts that the example `requirements.case` (a `{test}` edge) is supplied.
  - `only_edges_leaving_the_subject_contribute_inputs` asserts the same for `requirements.tester`.
  - The same test assesses `requirements.parent`, where `ready` refines it with `{impl}`, and asserts that `requirements.ready` is supplied.
  - `structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` asserts that the refining declaration `requirements.refined` is supplied with its full multi-paragraph text.
- **An `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone contributes no source text, except for structural assessments.**
  - The bundle test and `only_edges_leaving_the_subject_contribute_inputs` assert that `impl[Thing]/fn[run]` and `fn[run]` are absent.
  - `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` uses an `:impl:` anchor on `mod[inner]` and asserts that only the two `{test}` sources are supplied.
  - `structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest` covers the structural exception. It checks that the root `fn[api]` is supplied, deduplicated against its anchor, with no helper recursion. It also checks that a plain-text root is supplied, and that the structural flag is off in each non-structural case it sets up: a test reference, a test anchor, an example subject, a distributed requirement, and a refinement-only requirement.
- **Sources stay discoverable under the reference index.** `references_list_names_and_flattened_sites_without_recording_inputs` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` asserts `impl`, `test`, and `cite` sites by file and item. It also asserts that no inputs are recorded.
- **Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject do not contribute.** `only_edges_leaving_the_subject_contribute_inputs` asserts that `fn[helper]` and the citing example `requirements.citer` are absent. The tool test above shows the cite sites remain discoverable.
- **A `:test:` anchor contributes the complete file or the anchored node.**
  - `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs` asserts the whole file, with an exact input comparison.
  - `test_anchors_supply_only_the_selected_node` asserts the node only: sibling text is absent from the inputs and from the prompt.
- **An in-source `{test}` reference contributes the smallest enclosing outline node.**
  - Rust: `fn[test_ready]` and `fn[check]` are supplied, and the enclosing `impl[Thing]` is not.
  - Markdown outside a declaration: `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` asserts the `section[Usage]/paragraph@…` node.
  - Terminology declarations: `references_in_terminology_declarations_contribute_that_declaration` asserts that the definition is supplied as a whole and that `md/requirements.md` is not supplied as a section.
  - Other files: `notes.txt` is supplied as the complete file with item `""`.
  - Ownership: `markdown_references_select_the_nearest_directive_or_standalone_paragraph` in `src/inputs.rs` checks which node owns a reference.
- **Literal references, evidence copies, and generated output stay excluded.** `generated_evidence_references_are_omitted_by_default` asserts that `evidence/notes.md`, `evidence/copy.json`, and the string-literal `src/literal.rs` are absent. It also asserts that discovery still does not read `evidence/` after an explicit allow.
- **A `{fixme}` alone contributes no source.** `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` and `cited_built_ins_contribute_their_text_and_fixmes_in_own_sites_do_not` assert that acknowledgments are supplied with no containing-source inputs.
- **Only direct references count, with no recursive expansion.** The bundle test asserts that `requirements.distant` is not supplied even though the cited `requirements.base` cites it. It also asserts that earlier evidence inputs are not carried forward.

The last sentence of the requirement says reference links MUST NOT be described as proof that all relevant sources were found. It concerns static prompt wording, which `md/requirements/authoring.md` defines and which says to use targeted discovery. No conditional behavior carries it out. Other tests, such as `initial_prompt_conveys_when_to_choose_each_outcome`, check prompt wording separately. I count it as untestable under the exemption, not as a gap.

No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

except for structural assessments under

those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.

terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and

to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under

These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively

:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, and needs
no evidence input. Its issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Code implementations are reviewed as part of the definitions they implement or
test. Citation reviews assess cited source items and book passages under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.

:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} structural_inputs
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
:::{req} reference_index
The harness MUST expose a `references` tool with this interface:
```text
references({ selection: String?, roles: Array<"impl" | "cite" | "test">? }) -> ReferenceIndex
ReferenceIndex {
definitions: Array<DefinitionName>,
sites: Array<ReferenceSite>,
DefinitionName { name: String, kind: "requirement" | "example" }
ReferenceSite {
name: String,
role: "impl" | "cite" | "test",
file: String,
item: String?,
`selection` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`.
Without `selection`, the tool MUST return
the full name and kind of every requirement and named example in full-name
order, with empty `sites`. With `selection`, it MUST return the selected definitions
in full-name order and one flattened `sites` array containing every valid
reference to any match whose role is in `roles`, defaulting to
`["impl", "cite", "test"]`, under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, each naming the definition it
references, ordered by name, file, and position in the file, without line
numbers. Roles MUST be treated as a set: repeating a permitted role MUST NOT
duplicate sites or change the result.
An anchor under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` whose role is selected
by `roles` MUST be
reported as a site for its anchored file, with the anchored node's selector as
`item` when it names one and no `item` when it names the whole file. Every
other site MUST give as `item` the selector of its smallest enclosing outline
node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`. Only sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` MUST contribute sites. If reading such a
source fails, the tool MUST return an explanatory tool error naming the source.
An invalid selection or one matching no definition MUST return an explanatory tool
error.
An empty `roles` array MUST return no sites while preserving the selected
definitions' names and kinds. An unknown role or a value other than an array of
permitted role strings MUST return an explanatory tool error. Without `selection`,
`roles` MUST NOT change the definition-name listing.
Results MUST contain no requirement text, example text, reference commentary,
or source text. Like directory listings, they MUST
NOT become evidence inputs; the model requests the sources it relies on with the
`habeas` tool. For example,
`references({selection: "requirements.cli.status", roles: ["impl"]})` MUST
locate only that subject's implementation references and anchors, without
supplying their source or recording evidence inputs.
:::{req} source_tools
The harness MUST expose a `habeas` tool accepting exactly one of these request
forms. Each form MUST correspond to one existing evidence-input kind:
| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |
Selector arguments MUST use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Reads MUST use the current
project working tree, including unstaged changes to tracked files and staged new
files. By default, source inputs MUST stay within the project root after
resolving symlinks; in a Git worktree, both the requested file and its resolved
target MUST be present in the Git index. Projects outside Git MUST use the same
containment rules without requiring an index. Failure to read an existing
repository's index MUST be reported as an error.
The project-root `evidence/` directory MUST be excluded from model reads by
default, including symlink aliases. Every source the harness supplies to the
model MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`, and a denied model
read MUST return a tool error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
Line numbers are only a way to request sources; recorded evidence MUST identify
sources by outline selector and structural hash, never by line number. Request
line numbers MUST be one-based and inclusive, and omitting `line_end` MUST read
through EOF. A line-range request MUST be resolved to the innermost outline
nodes covering the requested lines, which are `line` nodes in a file using the
plain-text profile; the result MUST show the model each node's selector and
source text, without line numbers, and the harness MUST record those nodes as
outline inputs. The model-facing tool description MUST include the argument conventions
from the cited requirements, including outline selector syntax, definition
selections, and full definition names, with a short request example for each form.
A successful call MUST return the requested evidence input, populated by the
harness with the selected source text, using the existing evidence schema.
{cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
Required terminology dependencies MUST be returned alongside it as additional
definition inputs under {cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.
For item, requirement, and definition selections, the result MUST have this shape:
```text
HabeasResult {
input: EvidenceInput,
definitions: Array<DefinitionInput>,
Line-range selections can contain multiple outline nodes. Their result MUST use
`inputs: Array<EvidenceInput>` instead of the singular `input` field, including
when only one node is selected.
`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
harness MUST record inputs supplied to the model in the assessment's evidence.
A failed read MUST add no evidence input. Access-policy denials MUST be handled
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`; other failed reads MUST return
an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
